'''Shijiki Shrine''' (志々伎神社) is a Shinto shrine located in Nogomachi, {{ill|Hirado City|de|Stadt Hirado|ja|Hirado City}} in {{ill|Nagasaki Prefecture|de|Präfektur Nagasaki|ja|Nagasaki Prefecture}}. It is a shrine in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hizen Province]]. It is also referred to as Shijiki Shrine or Shiji Shrine. It holds the status of a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|lt=Small Shikinaisha}} and a {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|de|Modernes Schreinsystem|ja|近代社格制度|lt=Old Shrine Rank}} shrine, designating it as a prefectural shrine. Branch shrines exist throughout Kyushu under the names Shijiki, Shishiki, and Shiji, making it the largest among prefectural Shikinaisha. Ancient deity sumo, preserved here, is said to be the precursor to modern {{ill|Sumo|de|Sumo|ja|Sumo}}.<ref>[http://jlogos.com/docomosp/word.html?id=7221037 志々伎神社]. 角川日本地名大辞典.JLogos.com</ref><ref>“[https://web.archive.org/web/20030518172110/http://www53.tok2.com/home/nasubi/history/shjikijinja/shijikijinja3.html Shijiki Shrine Festival]”. Shijiki Shrine-3. Nasubi History Museum. As of May 18, 2003, the [http://www53.tok2.com/home/nasubi/history/shjikijinja/shijikijinja3.html Original]{{Broken link|date=2022年2月}} archive</ref> The Jangara, performed throughout Hirado Island, also spread from this shrine.

== Overview ==
It is said that the shrine was founded around the 5th century, though the exact date remains unknown. The sacred precinct centers on {{ill|Shijiki Mountain|de|Shijiki Berg|ja|Shijiki Mountain}} (with an elevation of 347.2 {{ill|meter|de|Meter|ja|meter}}) near the southern tip of {{ill|Hirado Island|de|Hirado-Insel|ja|Hirado Island}}. In ancient times, the upper shrine was located at the mountain summit, the middle shrine on the mid-slope, and the ground shrine (also known as the lower shrine or Hentomiyashiro) was situated in the fishing village of Miyano-ura at the foot, while an offshore shrine was placed on an islet off Miyano-ura. In addition, a bettō-ji known as Enman-ji was established.
The enshrined deity is the son of {{ill|Yamato Takeru|de|Yamato Takeru|ja|Yamato Takeru}}, and the half-brother of {{ill|Emperor Chūai|de|Kaiser Chūai|ja|Emperor Chūai}}. He is said to have followed {{ill|Empress Jingū|de|Kaiserin Jingū|ja|Empress Jingū}} in the {{ill|Campaigns against the Three Han|de|Drei-Han-Feldzüge|ja|Campaigns against the Three Han}}, later remaining in the area and being commissioned to guard the western regions, known as {{ill|Jūjōbetsu-Ō|de|Jūjōbetsu-Ō|ja|Jūjōbetsu-Ō}} ({{ill|Jūjōbetsu-no-mikoto|de|Jūjōbetsu-no-mikoto|ja|Jūjōbetsu-no-mikoto}})). The ground shrine is said to have repurposed an armory established by the king, while the offshore shrine is believed to mark his tomb.

In the Divine Name List of the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|Engi-shiki}}, within {{ill|Hizen Province|de|Provinz Hizen|ja|Hizen Province}}, it is listed as one of the four {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|ja|Shikinaisha}}; it is the only shrine of its kind in Nagasaki Prefecture, excluding the Iki and Tsushima regions, and is the oldest known shrine. It has long garnered widespread reverence from the {{ill|Matsuura Faction|de|Matsuura Fraktion|ja|Matsuura Faction}} and local fishermen.

The current center of worship is the middle shrine. Originally, the shrine was housed in a small structure at the foot of Shijiki Mountain’s summit, but it was relocated to the mid-slope in {{ill|Yōroku|de|Yōroku|ja|Yōroku}} 2 ({{ill|1559|ab|1559|af|1559|als|1559|am|1559 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1559|ar|1559|ary|1559|arz|1559|ast|1559|avk|1559|az|1559|azb|۱۵۵۹ (میلادی)|bar|1559|bcl|1559|be|1559|be_x_old|1559|bg|1559|bn|১৫৫৯|bpy|মারি ১৫৫৯|br|1559|bs|1559.|ca|1559|cdo|1559 nièng|ceb|1559|ckb|١٥٥٩|crh|1559|cs|1559|cv|1559|cy|1559|da|1559|de|1559|diq|1559|el|1559|eml|1559|eo|1559|es|1559|et|1559|eu|1559|fa|۱۵۵۹ (میلادی)|fi|1559|fo|1559|fr|1559|frr|1559|fur|1559|fy|1559|ga|1559|gan|1559年|gcr|1559|gd|1559|gl|1559|he|1559|hi|१५५९|hr|1559.|ht|1559 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1559|hy|1559|ia|1559|id|1559|ilo|1559|io|1559|is|1559|it|1559|ja|1559年|jv|1559|ka|1559|kaa|1559|kk|1559 жыл|ko|1559년|krc|1559 джыл|la|1559|lb|1559|lfn|1559|lij|1559|lmo|1559|lt|1559 m.|lv|1559. gads|mai|१५५९|map_bms|1559|mdf|1559|mg|1559|mhr|1559|mi|1559|min|1559|mk|1559|mr|इ.स. १५५९|mrj|1559 и|ms|1559|my|၁၅၅၉|mzn|۱۵۵۹|nah|1559|nap|1559|nds|1559|new|सन् १५५९|nl|1559|nn|1559|no|1559|nrm|1559|nso|1559|oc|1559|or|୧୫୫୯|os|1559-æм аз|pa|1559|pl|1559|pnb|1559|pt|1559|qu|1559|ro|1559|ru|1559 год|rue|1559|sa|१५५९|sah|1559|scn|1559|sd|1559ع|se|1559|sh|1559.|shn|1559|simple|1559|sk|1559|sl|1559|smn|1559|sq|1559|sr|1559|su|1559|sv|1559|sw|1559|ta|1559|tg|Соли 1559|th|พ.ศ. 2102|tk|1559|tl|1559|tly|1559|tr|1559|tt|1559 ел|uk|1559|ur|1559ء|uz|1559|vec|1559|vi|1559|vls|1559|wa|1559|war|1559|wuu|1559年|xmf|1559|yi|1559|zh|1559年|zh_min_nan|1559 nî|zh_yue|1559年|qid=Q6609}}). Furthermore, in {{ill|1961|de|1961|ja|1961年12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1961}} ({{ill|Showa|de|Showa|ja|Showa}} 36), it was moved to its present location, which occupies the former site of Enman-ji—a bettō-ji abolished in the early Meiji period under the {{ill|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Edict|de|Trennung von Shinto und Buddhismus Dekret|ja|Shinto-Buddhism Separation Edict}}.

The former shrine grounds were designated as a historical site of Nagasaki Prefecture in {{ill|1974|de|1974|ja|1974}} (Showa 49), under the name "Former Shikinaisha Shijiki Shrine Site."
